new.n: Train robber George Smalley's missing loot, McBain
new.pl: GNIS McBain (village), Missaukee County; the house where he was killed is not located
new.st: George A. Smalley, a former McBain resident accused in a Chicago & West Michigan train robbery and a shooting near Grand Rapids, got off the train at McBain and was shot dead by a sheriff's posse in Aug 1895. No money was found on him. Later treasure write-ups say the loot was hidden near Farwell or McBain.
new.t: The robbery and killing are in print; the hidden-loot part is only a modern write-up. Find the house where he died on an 1890s Missaukee plat before any search. Private: permission.
src: Alma Record, 30 Aug 1895 (Library of Congress, Chronicling America)
Treasure listicle (web) for the hidden-loot claim
pinev: Town-level: GNIS McBain; the house is not located.

new.n: Stolen Mattrick money: "upwards of $5,000" said still buried on the farm near Beaver
new.pl: GNIS Beaver (Marinette County); the Mattrick farm is not yet placed (needs a c.1912-25 Beaver Twp plat)
new.st: In 1924 about $11,200 was stolen from farmer Gottlieb Mattrick by a relative, who pleaded guilty. About $3,000 was recovered buried on the farm and several thousand more turned up in Minneapolis. In Apr 1925 the thief's lawyers said upwards of $5,000 remained buried 'twenty feet west of a small birch tree on the Mattrick farm and about thirty paces to the left of' the $3,000 hole. On a Saturday night 22 men dug by flashlight under armed guard, joined by the sheriff's men, and found nothing.
new.t: D: the 1924 court record says $6,000 was found buried on the farm and the rest was invested in St. Paul; the 1925 'still buried' claim came via lawyers and is one wire story. No later recovery reported 1925-40. If placed, search west of the old recovery hole; the 1925 birch is long gone. Private: permission.
src: Eau Claire Leader-Telegram, 29 Apr 1925, p. 1, 'Think Treasure Still on Farm'
Wausau Daily Herald, 27 Apr 1925, p. 1, 'Fail to Find Buried Money Near Marinette'
pinev: Placeholder at GNIS Beaver; the farm is not yet placed.
